newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, top ministers to discuss reform policy.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, top ministers to discuss reform policy.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will meet top members of his government on Tuesday to discuss the course of reforms, the Kremlin press service said.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his two first deputies, Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, will take part in the meeting along with Valentin Yumashev, who heads Yeltsin's administration.
Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said on Monday the meeting would start at noon (0800 GMT) to review the government's record in the first six months of the year.
Yeltsin reshuffled the government dramatically in March, putting reformers like Chubais, 41, and Nemtsov, 37, into key positions to reinvigorate market reforms under veteran Chernomyrdin.
He has called the previous cabinet "stagnant" and has given the new government strong support in its efforts to put state finances in order, reorganise natural monopolies and fight corruption.

The government says it has met Yeltsin's demands and paid off a huge backlog of pensions by Tuesday. Chernomyrdin said on Monday the next priority would be the armed forces, where discontent is rife over non-payment of salaries and general decline.

One of the issues likely to emerge at the meeting on Tuesday is resistance from the opposition-dominated State Duma, the lower house of parliament, to a package of market reform legislation proposed by the cabinet.

The Duma went on holiday last week until September 1 after rejecting cabinet proposals to cut 1997 budget spending across the board because of revenue shortfalls, and to slash some social benefits -- a legacy of Soviet paternalism the government says it can no longer afford.
Yeltsin and Chubais, both known for a tough line towards the Duma, have said the government will pursue its policy regardless of whether it has the legislature's backing.

But Chernomyrdin took a slightly more conciliatory line on Monday, saying the cabinet needed the Duma's support and promising to try to persuade deputies to interrupt their holiday and consider the most pressing draft bills in July.
Chernomyrdin is expected to meet Duma speaker Gennady Seleznyov on Tuesday to discuss the situation.
